 More than 900 state security personnel were assigned to protect spectators and maintain order during the Clásico de la 57 between Atlético de San Luis and Querétaro at Estadio Libertad Financiera on October 20, 2026. The State Civil Guard announced that the operation would begin at 3 p.m., six hours before the scheduled 7 p.m. Liga MX kickoff.
 According to the State Civil Guard, the deployment formed part of the Estadio Seguro security operation. Authorities called on supporters to cooperate with officers and help prevent incidents during the regional rivalry, which has previously been affected by violence among fans. The security measures accompanied a fixture between neighboring clubs whose rivalry dates to 1957 and has developed through decisive promotion battles, memorable results and matches across multiple levels of Mexican soccer.

 Atlético de San Luis entered the October 20 match following a 1-1 draw against Toluca at Estadio Nemesio Diez. Querétaro arrived after losing 5-0 to Santos Laguna in Torreón, according to Atlético de San Luis's official match preview.

 Adonai Escobedo was appointed referee for the match, with Marco Bisguerra and Michel Espinoza serving as assistant referees. Óscar Mejía was designated the fourth official. The rivalry takes its name from Federal Highway 57, a major route connecting San Luis Potosí and Querétaro. According to Plano Informativo, the teams first met on August 25, 1957, during celebrations honoring San Luis Rey de Francia, with the San Luis side winning 1-0.
 One of the rivalry's most significant chapters came in June 2005, when the clubs contested a promotion final for a place in Mexico's top division. Querétaro won the first leg 2-1, forcing San Luis to overturn the deficit in the return match at Estadio Alfonso Lastras. Héctor Giménez scored early for San Luis, and Ariel González headed the decisive goal during extra time. The 2-0 victory gave San Luis a 3-2 aggregate win and secured promotion, making the final a defining moment for the club and its supporters.
 Other notable meetings include a 4-4 draw in 2003 and Querétaro's 1-0 defeat against San Luis in the Copa MX in January 2015, when Brazilian World Cup winner Ronaldinho featured for Querétaro. Diego Cervantes scored the only goal in that match. The rivalry also has a history of security concerns.

 On October 20, 2019, a match at Estadio Alfonso Lastras was suspended following clashes between supporters, prompting sanctions and renewed attention to stadium safety. Recent results have continued to shape the rivalry. San Luis won 2-0 in March 2023 and 4-0 in August 2024, while Querétaro secured a 1-0 victory in February 2025 and won a five-goal contest 3-2 in August that year.
 San Luis claimed another victory on February 14, 2026, beating Querétaro 3-0 at Estadio Alfonso Lastras through goals from João Pedro, Jesús Medina and Miguel García. The October 20 meeting added another Liga MX fixture to a rivalry with nearly seven decades of history.
